players.product: industrial & electronics gases (N2, He, specialty) for fabs

quarterly_data.signal: Traditional industrial gas backlog of approximately $3 billion in projects (FID-approved, long-term contracts); a significant portion of the capital projected for the backlog will support electronic customers, including over $1.5 billion in project wins for Air Products in the last six months. Two very large projects were announced, one in Korea and one in Taiwan, and other projects are to be announced this quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog ~$3 billion; over $1.5 billion of project wins in last six months

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Eduardo Menezes: the market is going through a super cycle and the opportunity list is skewed to the electronic side - probably close to two-thirds of opportunities or more are in the electronic space; electronics is where the growth is, versus replacement-driven opportunities in chemicals and steel. Air Products kept the capability to execute electronics projects in Asia, which fits where the market is now.
quarterly_data.figure: close to two-thirds or more of opportunities in electronics

quarterly_data.signal: One very large multi-phase project in Taiwan started in 2022 is building more than five large air separation plants: three are done and two are still to go. All other backlog projects have basically come in the last 12 months.
quarterly_data.figure: Taiwan project: more than five large air separation plants, three done, two to go

quarterly_data.signal: Helium: headwind of 2% in the quarter, better than the 3% guided, driven by improved volume and pricing in Asia supporting electronic customers; 40% of all helium volume sold in the quarter came from the Texas cavern (more in June) as Qatar-sourced volumes remain very limited and are excluded from the forecast. Air Products has been gaining many new long-term helium volume commitments, especially in electronics and especially in Asia, some tied to new electronics projects starting in one to three years and carrying the same term as its large on-site contracts.
quarterly_data.figure: helium headwind 2% (guided 3%); 40% of helium volume from Texas cavern

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 FY2026: sales up 5%, operating income up 9%, operating margin 25.6% (up over 100 basis points), EPS $3.47 up 12%, return on capital 11.7%. Volume growth led by on-site, new assets coming on stream in Asia and the Americas and helium; new assets contributed a 3% year-on-year benefit, with electronics ramping strongly from both backlog and supply and green shoots in Asia specific to the electronic space.
quarterly_data.figure: sales +5%; operating income +9%; operating margin 25.6%; EPS $3.47 (+12%)

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal full-year EPS guidance raised to $13.39-$13.49, an 11%-12% increase from the prior year; Q4 EPS expected at $3.55-$3.65, up 5%-8%. Helium expected to remain a headwind on lower price despite volume and price improvement in Asia.

Capital discipline: targeting approximately $1.5 billion per year going forward in traditional industrial gas projects (air separation and hydrogen), with fiscal 2026 capex now approximately $3.5 billion (reduced by about $500 million on payment timing, lower maintenance and canceled projects); the exit from the Louisiana and Casa Grande, Arizona clean-energy projects (pre-tax charge of $2.9 billion) lets Air Products focus investment on the backlog of traditional industrial gas projects, especially the electronics end market.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$1.5 billion per year traditional industrial gas capex; FY2026 capex ~$3.5 billion; $2.9 billion charge

quarterly_data.signal: Merchant markets: Americas progressing well, Europe difficult, China still difficult with overcapacity; Taiwan and South Korea suffering from high energy costs outside of electronics, where Air Products does not have big exposure. Share buybacks come into line of sight toward the end of 2027 / beginning of 2028 after high-return projects and dividend growth.
